mainTopic: Whether waiting for sunset counts as 'missing' a step in the hidden-grave and יולדת cases, and a new משנה on finding buried corpses
overview: רב המנונא rules that a נזיר and someone bringing a קרבן פסח who walked over a hidden grave (קבר התהום) on the seventh day of their purification stay pure, because טומאת התהום is too weak to undo what they did. רבא challenges him from a משנה that says someone still in חזקת טמא stays impure. רב המנונא concedes about the נזיר, who still has to shave, and רבא concedes about the עושה פסח, who is missing no action. אביי objects that the עושה פסח still has to wait for sunset (הערב שמש). רבא answers that the sun sets by itself, so waiting for it does not count as something missing. The גמרא then shows that אביי later accepted this, using a ברייתא about a woman who miscarried on or before יום מלאת. There, רב כהנא asks why a woman who must wait for sunset counts as complete, and אביי himself answers that the sun sets by itself. A new משנה then begins: one or two corpses found in a new place may be removed with their surrounding earth, but three corpses spaced four to eight אמות apart make the place a שכונת קברות.

steps.title: רב המנונא: A hidden grave does not undo purity on the seventh day
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא rules that a נזיר or someone bringing a קרבן פסח who passed over a hidden grave on their seventh day of purification stays pure, because טומאת התהום is not strong enough to cancel what they did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: A נזיר and a person bringing the קרבן פסח who walked over a hidden grave on their seventh day are pure. Why? Because the impurity of a hidden grave is not strong enough to cancel their actions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא gives a lenient ruling: people in the last stage of becoming pure are not set back by a grave that was only discovered later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These people are on day seven of purifying from טומאת מת, so they are almost, but not fully, pure. If they later learn they passed over a hidden grave, you might think their קרבנות are ruined. רב המנונא says no: hidden-grave impurity (טומאת התהום) is a weak kind of impurity, and it cannot cancel (לְמִיסְתַּר) their נזירות or their פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: A hidden grave nobody knew about, found only later
Impurity from a hidden grave, treated more leniently

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:
A nazirite and one performing the Paschal offering
who walked by a grave in the depths
phrases.notes: A "grave in the depths" is a grave nobody knew about. It was discovered only afterward.

phrases.english: on their seventh day — they are pure.
phrases.notes: He means the seventh day of their purification from טומאת מת, before they have fully finished becoming pure.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the impurity of the depths is not strong enough to cancel.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר or עושה פסח on their seventh day who passed over a קבר התהום stays pure, because טומאת התהום cannot cancel their actions.

steps.title: רבא challenges from the משנה about presumptive impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the משנה: someone going to immerse to purify from טומאת מת is still impure, because whoever is in a state of impurity (חזקת טמא) stays impure. The same should apply to people on their seventh day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: If someone went down to purify himself from corpse impurity, he is impure, because one who is presumed impure stays impure, and one who is presumed pure stays pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב המנונא's ruling with a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that the leniency of טומאת התהום only helps someone who was already pure. A person still in the middle of purifying from טומאת מת is in חזקת טמא, so a hidden grave does make him impure. A נזיר or עושה פסח on day seven has not finished purifying, so they should be impure too.

keyTerms.meaning: A person's default status of impurity
A person's default status of purity

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying hidden-grave impurity is never lenient. It is saying the leniency helps only someone who was already pure, not someone still in the middle of becoming pure.

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
If he descended to purify himself from corpse impurity — he is impure,
since one presumed impure remains impure,
and one presumed pure remains pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב המנונא's ruling from step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's ruling that people on the seventh day stay pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People on day seven are still in חזקת טמא, and the משנה says such a person is made impure even by טומאת התהום.

steps.title: רב המנונא concedes regarding the נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא agrees that a נזיר is impure in this case, because he still has to shave (מחוסר תגלחת). He keeps his ruling for the עושה פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said to him: I agree with you about a נזיר, since he is still missing the shaving.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא partly gives in. He admits the משנה's rule applies to the נזיר, but not to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר who became impure must shave his head as part of becoming pure. Until he does that, he is clearly still in חזקת טמא, so the משנה applies to him. By saying this, רב המנונא narrows his ruling to the עושה פסח, who has no such action left.

keyTerms.meaning: The shaving a נזיר does after becoming impure

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב המנונא answering רבא.

phrases.english: I agree with you regarding a nazirite,
who is lacking shaving.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge by conceding part of it
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial concession that limits the original ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling covered both the נזיר and the עושה פסח
steps.terutzMaskana: The נזיר, who still needs תגלחת, is in חזקת טמא and is impure. The ruling stands only for the עושה פסח.

steps.title: רבא concedes regarding the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבא agrees in return that the עושה פסח is pure, since he is not missing any action.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: I too agree with you about one bringing the קרבן פסח, since he is not missing anything at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא meets רב המנונא halfway and accepts the ruling about the קרבן פסח person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עושה פסח has no further action to do on his body, so on day seven he can already be treated as basically pure. So the משנה's case of חזקת טמא does not apply to him. Now both אמוראים agree: the נזיר is impure and the עושה פסח is pure.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֲנָא מוֹדֵינָא לָךְ בְּעוֹשֵׂה פֶסַח,
phrases.english: I too agree with you regarding one performing the Paschal offering,
since he is not lacking anything at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא אַף אֲנָא מוֹדֵינָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא answers רב המנונא's concession with a concession of his own
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עושה פסח who passed over a קבר התהום on day seven is pure, because he lacks no action.

steps.title: אביי objects that the עושה פסח still needs sunset
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא: the עושה פסח is still missing something, namely sunset (הערב שמש) on the seventh day.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But he is missing sunset!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions רבא's claim that the קרבן פסח person is 'not missing anything.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Full purity only comes after sunset on day seven. So the עושה פסח also seems to be missing a step, just like the נזיר, and he should also count as חזקת טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, isn't it so that

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But he is lacking sunset!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי וְהָא מְחוּסָּר הֶעֱרֵב שֶׁמֶשׁ
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the עושה פסח lacks nothing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He still needs הערב שמש to be fully pure, so he is also 'lacking' something.

steps.title: רבא: sunset happens by itself
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that sunset comes on its own, so waiting for it is not a real 'missing' step like the נזיר's shaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The sun sets by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his position: the only thing that counts as 'missing' is an action the person has to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נזיר is missing an action he must perform, his תגלחת. Sunset requires nothing from the person and will happen anyway. So the עושה פסח is not considered lacking, and he stays pure.
steps.whatToRemember: A נזיר on day seven who passed over a קבר התהום is impure, because he still needs to shave. An עושה פסח is pure, because his only remaining 'step', sunset, happens by itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a key line: only a missing action (מחוסר מעשה) keeps someone in חזקת טמא, not just waiting for time to pass.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The sun sets by itself.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a distinction between a missing action and something that happens on its own
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sunset counts as something missing, like shaving
steps.terutzMaskana: Sunset happens automatically, so it is not a 'lack'. The עושה פסח stays pure.

steps.title: אביי also changes his mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that אביי retracted his challenge and accepted רבא's view, and it introduces a ברייתא as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even אביי retracted, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that אביי came around to רבא's answer. It is now setting up a ברייתא that will be connected to this change of mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5 אביי argued that waiting for sunset counts as 'missing' something. In Step 6 רבא answered that it does not. Now we learn that אביי himself gave up his challenge, and the word דתניא signals that a teaching is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back on his words, he retracted

phrases.english: And even Abaye retracted, as it is taught:
phrases.notes: He retracted his challenge from before, that waiting for sunset counts as 'missing' something.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports that the challenger of Step 5 accepted רבא's answer in Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי accepted רבא's position that waiting for sunset is not a real 'missing' step.

steps.title: Miscarriage on the day of completion versus during the days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that a miscarriage on יום מלאת requires its own קרבן, while a miscarriage during the days of purity does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she miscarried on the day of completion, she brings another קרבן. If it was during the days before completion, she does not bring another one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its basic rule about a woman who gave birth and then miscarried before bringing her קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day the days of purity end (יום מלאת) is the day she becomes obligated to bring her קרבן. A miscarriage on that day counts as a new event that needs its own קרבן. A miscarriage before that day is covered by the one קרבן she will already bring.

keyTerms.meaning: The day her days of purity are completed, when the קרבן becomes due
During the days, before they are completed

phrases.english: On the day of completion, she brings.
phrases.notes: She brings a separate קרבן for the miscarriage, on top of the one for the birth.

phrases.english: During the completion, she does not bring.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם מְלֹאת תָּבִיא תּוֹךְ מְלֹאת לֹא תָּבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the ברייתא that Step 7 introduced with דתניא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about a יולדת who miscarried on or before יום מלאת

steps.title: A possible mistaken reading
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a mistaken idea: maybe a later miscarriage after the first completion lets her bring one קרבן that covers both obligations.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: she does not bring for a birth that happened before the completion, but she does bring for a birth that happened after the completion, and that one קרבן frees her from both.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא suggests a 'you might have thought' idea. It is setting up the next move, where a פסוק will reject this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a woman who miscarried again, after her first days of purity ended but while the days for the earlier miscarriage were still running. The suggestion is that she brings a new קרבן for this later miscarriage, and that it covers both the birth and the miscarriage.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might think', introducing an idea that will be rejected
And she is freed from both obligations

phrases.english: One might think she does not bring
for a birth that was before the completion,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל תָּבִיא עַל לֵידָה שֶׁלְּאַחַר מְלֹאת,
phrases.english: but she does bring for a birth that was after the completion,
and she is exempt from both —
phrases.notes: Both means the earlier obligation and the new one, covered by a single קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא תָּבִיא עַל לֵידָה שֶׁלִּפְנֵי מְלֹאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible extension of the rule in Step 8 that the ברייתא will reject.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a miscarriage after the first completion, but within the days of the earlier miscarriage, require its own קרבן?

steps.title: The פסוק limits the extra קרבן to the day of completion itself
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'וּבִמְלֹאת יְמֵי טׇהֳרָה' teaches that only a miscarriage on יום מלאת brings a separate קרבן, and one during the days does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And when the days of her purity are completed.' On the day of completion she brings. During the completion she does not bring.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the 'you might think' idea from Step 9 by quoting a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'when the days of her purity are completed' tie the extra קרבן to the actual day of completion. So if the miscarriage happened while the days of purity of an earlier miscarriage were still running, she does not bring an extra קרבן, even if her first days had already ended.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches', introducing the פסוק that settles the question

steps.whatToRemember: The extra קרבן depends on the day of completion (יום מלאת) itself. A miscarriage during the days (תוך מלאת) is covered without another קרבן.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And when the days of her purity are completed."
On the day of completion, she brings,
during the completion, she does not bring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea raised in Step 9 by using a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. Only a miscarriage on יום מלאת brings a separate קרבן. One that happens during the days of purity does not.

steps.title: רב כהנא explains why the days of purity are different
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that a miscarriage during the ימי טהרה brings no separate קרבן, because during those days she is still missing the ability to bring her קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Here it is different, because she is lacking the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives the reason behind the ברייתא's rule from Step 10. A miscarriage during the ימי טהרה does not bring its own קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the ימי טהרה the woman is not yet allowed to bring her קרבן. Since that step is still 'missing', a second birth in that window cannot start a new, separate obligation. It simply joins the first one.

keyTerms.meaning: She is lacking; something is still missing

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: Here it is different,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means a miscarriage during the days of purity, the case from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: because she is lacking the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the ברייתא's distinction in Step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A miscarriage during the ימי טהרה creates no new קרבן obligation, because she is still unable to bring her קרבן

steps.title: But on the day of completion she is also missing something
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא challenges his own reason. On יום מלאת she also cannot bring her קרבן yet, because she still needs הערב שמש. So why does a miscarriage on that day need a separate קרבן?
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, she is lacking sunset!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא attacks the reason he just gave. The same kind of 'missing step' seems to exist on יום מלאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'still missing something' means no new obligation, the יום מלאת case should work the same way, since she must wait for sunset. Yet the ברייתא rules that a miscarriage on יום מלאת does need its own קרבן. This brings back the same question אביי raised about the עושה פסח in Step 5, which רבא answered in Step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunset; waiting for the sun to set

phrases.english: There too, she is lacking sunset!
phrases.notes: 'There' means a miscarriage on יום מלאת, the very day her days of purity are completed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's reason that a 'missing' step blocks a new קרבן obligation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On יום מלאת she is also missing something, namely sunset. By the same logic she should need no separate קרבן, but the ברייתא says she does.

steps.title: אביי: sunset happens by itself
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that waiting for sunset is not a real 'missing' step, because sunset comes on its own. This is the very reasoning of רבא, which shows that אביי accepted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The sun sets by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב כהנא's challenge. In doing so, he uses the same argument רבא made in Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A missing קרבן needs a person to act, but sunset needs nothing, so it does not count as 'missing'. That is why יום מלאת is treated as already complete and a new miscarriage brings a new קרבן. Because אביי argues this himself, the גמרא has its proof that he retracted his challenge, as reported in Step 7.
steps.whatToRemember: A step that happens by itself, like sunset, does not count as 'missing'. A step that needs action, like bringing a קרבן, does. אביי says this himself, which proves he accepted רבא's view.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the proof from Step 7. It shows that אביי really did adopt רבא's reasoning from the עושה פסח case.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
The sun sets by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: שִׁימְשָׁא מִמֵּילָא עָרְבָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between a missing step that needs action and one that happens automatically
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Waiting for sunset is a 'missing' step just like a missing קרבן
steps.terutzMaskana: Sunset comes on its own, so it is not considered missing. יום מלאת counts as complete, and a miscarriage then needs its own קרבן.

steps.title: New משנה: finding one or two buried corpses
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who finds a corpse for the first time, buried in the usual way, may move it along with the earth around it. The same applies to two corpses.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who finds a corpse for the first time, lying in the usual way, removes it and its surrounding earth. If he finds two, he removes them and their surrounding earth.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: what to do when you discover a buried מת. If there are only one or two, you may remove them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'For the first time' means the place was not already known as a graveyard. One or two corpses do not make the area a graveyard, so they may be moved. The earth around them (תפוסה) is taken too, because it is part of the burial.

keyTerms.meaning: For the first time; in a place not known as a graveyard
Lying in the usual way of burial

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who finds a corpse for the first time,
lying in its usual manner,
he removes it and its surrounding earth.
Two — he removes them and their surrounding earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One or two corpses found in a new place, buried in the usual way, may be removed together with their surrounding earth

steps.title: Three corpses spaced apart make a graveyard
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that three corpses found four to eight אמות apart from each other count as a שכונת קברות, a graveyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found three, and there are four to eight cubits between one and the next, this is a graveyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the case of three corpses. Spaced the right way, they show that the place is a graveyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With three corpses at regular spacing of four to eight אמות, the pattern looks like a planned graveyard. So the place is no longer treated as a few loose graves. It gets the status of a שכונת קברות.

keyTerms.meaning: A graveyard; a neighborhood of graves

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the number three alone makes a graveyard. The משנה requires both three corpses and a spacing of four to eight אמות between them.

phrases.english: If he found three,
if there is between this one and that one
from four cubits up to eight,
this is a graveyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָצָא שְׁלֹשָׁה, אִם יֵשׁ בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, contrasting three corpses with one or two
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three corpses spaced four to eight אמות apart establish the place as a שכונת קברות
